I am a young woman, alone most of the day on this small piece of land my husband and I own. Last season I got the coupon from the government, and I pray I get it again this year — without it I cannot buy fertilizer, the bag is too dear. If the coupon comes, I will put one bag of 23-21-0 when the maize is small, then one bag of urea when it is knee-high, same as my mother showed me and same as my neighbor does. I plant the seed they give me with the coupon, it is the good one that grows tall, and between the maize rows I put my groundnuts like every year. I keep a little heap of sweepings and goat droppings by the house and I carry it in a basin to the planting holes — it is not much but it helps where the soil is tired. I cannot buy medicine for the crop, and water I wait from the sky like everybody. The work is mine and my husband's, and my sister comes when she can at weeding time — I do not have money to pay anyone.
